claims.text: The starting material is gas-atomized FeCoNiCrAl powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Earlier HVAF-M3 work used the same 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces acceptable-quality FeCoNiCrAl coatings but insufficient thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 oxygen/fuel gas-flow rates will increase in-flight particle velocity.
A spray distance around 300–350 mm is a suitable nozzle-specific optimum for the proposed HVAF-i7 FeCoNiCrAl process.
Higher particle velocity gives the particles greater kinetic energy.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves impact, flattening, and particle-to-substrate interfacial bonding.
Improved particle impact and bonding will produce a denser and thicker coating buildup.
Increasing particle velocity reduces in-flight deceleration and premature particle cooling.
The proposed velocity increase will reduce in-flight oxidation.
Higher particle velocity will increase deposition efficiency.
The adjusted process will significantly increase coating thickness relative to the unadjusted HVAF-i7 baseline.
The thicker coating will retain acceptable adhesion, coating integrity, and low as-sprayed oxidation.
FeCoNiCrAl-family thermal-sprayed coatings can exhibit useful elevated-temperature oxidation or wear performance.
The adjusted coating will remain durable during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition inside diameters as small as 120 mm.
Thermal-spray processing can change the phase constitution of FeCoNiCrAl-family material relative to its powder or as-cast state.
High temperature, oxygen concentration, and powder surface area can promote in-flight oxidation during thermal spraying, making excessive oxidation a relevant process boundary.
Spray distances established for conventional MCrAlY coatings may not translate directly to HVAF-i7 spraying of FeCoNiCrAl.
